full_judgment: 7. Mr. Probir Neogi, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that the High Court Division failed to consider that the plaintiffs failed to prove the existence of the probate case and while the trial Court during trial called for the records of the pro-bate case, the concerned office could not produce the records and it transpires that the Will as well as probate case is totally false and forged. He further submitted that the plaintiffs claimed that Satish Chandra Roy executed a Will in favour of his daughter Purna Shashi Dasya on 03.01.1962 by appointing Subol Chandra Das as executor and they got probate on 01.07.63, but at that time the legal heirs of Satish Chandra Roy were not made party in the probate proceeding, and as such the probate was illegal and no right accrued in favour of Purna Shashi against the right of inheritance of Narayan Chandra Roy, and as such the impugned judgement and decree is illegal and cannot be sustained in law. He also submitted that the High Court Division failed to notice that the daughter of the executor of the Will had no right to transfer any land to any body and daughter of Satish Mohan did not execute any deed in favour of the plaintiffs and even did not give any power for which the plaintiffs never acquired any right, title and interest in the suit land and as such the instant suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession is not maintainable, but the High Court Division erred in decreeing the suit and thus the same is liable to be set aside.
